shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Separates instrument panels and cards from the bench background.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Resting shadow on buttons and the brand/drop-zone marks; deepens on hover, flattens on active press.

shadows.name: control-lift-hover
shadows.purpose: Hover state for control-lift; pairs with a 1px upward translateY.

shadows.name: control-lift-active
shadows.purpose: Active/pressed state for control-lift; pairs with a 1px downward translateY.

shadows.name: state-glow
shadows.purpose: Halo around the current stage dot in the job-path tracker (error variant uses --error-soft).

motion.name: control-transition

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid control-blue action button; the only fully-filled interactive surface in the system.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.58rem 1rem; background: #1769e0; border: 1px solid #1769e0; border-radius: 7px; box-shadow: 0 3px 8px rgba(26,39,52,0.18); color: #ffffff; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms ease-out, border-color 160ms ease-out, box-shadow 160ms ease-out, transform 160ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0e4fae; border-color: #0e4fae; box-shadow: 0 5px 13px rgba(26,39,52,0.18); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { box-shadow: 0 2px 5px rgba(26,39,52,0.18); transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1769e0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Outlined button for non-destructive secondary actions (Cancel, Download all files).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.58rem 1rem; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #788592; border-radius: 7px; color: #111820; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms ease-out, border-color 160ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: #e9eef1; border-color: #1769e0; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1769e0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Danger Button
components.description: Transparent, red-outlined button reserved for destructive actions (Delete job).
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-width: 44px; min-height: 44px; padding: 0.58rem 1rem; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #ad2a22; border-radius: 7px; box-shadow: none; color: #ad2a22; font-weight: 700; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 160ms ease-out; } .ds-btn-danger:hover { background: #ffebe8; } .ds-btn-danger:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1769e0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Small uppercase state chip on work-order cards and job headers; ok/error/busy are the only three states.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: fit-content; min-height: 1.7rem; padding: 0.2rem 0.58rem; border: 1px solid #788592; border-radius: 3px; font-size: 0.68rem; font-weight: 800; letter-spacing: 0.055em; line-height: 1; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge--ok { background: #e3f4eb; border-color: #14784f; color: #14784f; } .ds-badge--error { background: #ffebe8; border-color: #ad2a22; color: #ad2a22; } .ds-badge--busy { background: #e4efff; border-color: #1769e0; color: #0e4fae; }

components.name: Instrument Panel
components.description: The base panel shell: a pale inspection-sheet surface lifted off the bench with a static accent rule across its top edge.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; padding: clamp(1rem, 3vw, 1.65rem); background: #f8f9f7; border: 1px solid #788592; border-radius: 7px; box-shadow: 0 9px 24px rgba(26,39,52,0.18); } .ds-panel::before { content: ""; position: absolute; inset-block-start: -1px; inset-inline: 1.25rem; height: 3px; background: #1769e0; border-radius: 0 0 3px 3px; } .ds-panel h2 { margin: 0; font-size: clamp(1.35rem, 1.1rem + 1vw, 2rem); letter-spacing: -0.035em; }

components.name: Job Path Stage Tracker
components.description: Signature component: a fixed 5-stage horizontal tracker with a connecting line, reporting the literal Inspect, Configure, Convert, Validate, and Download path.
components.html:
1. Inspect
  2. Configure
  3. Convert
  4. Validate
  5. Download
components.css: .ds-job-path { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 0; list-style: none; margin: 1.25rem 0; padding: 0; } .ds-stage { position: relative; display: grid; justify-items: center; gap: 0.35rem; color: #52616f; font-size: clamp(0.63rem, 2.4vw, 0.76rem); font-weight: 700; text-align: center; } .ds-stage::before, .ds-stage::after { content: ""; position: absolute; inset-block-start: 0.42rem; height: 2px; background: #c8d0d6; } .ds-stage::before { inset-inline: 0 50%; } .ds-stage::after { inset-inline: 50% 0; } .ds-stage:first-child::before, .ds-stage:last-child::after { display: none; } .ds-stage-mark { position: relative; z-index: 1; width: 0.95rem; height: 0.95rem; background: #f8f9f7; border: 2px solid #788592; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-stage--complete { color: #111820; } .ds-stage--complete::before, .ds-stage--complete::after { background: #14784f; } .ds-stage--complete .ds-stage-mark { background: #14784f; border-color: #14784f; } .ds-stage--current { color: #0e4fae !important; } .ds-stage--current .ds-stage-mark { background: #1769e0; border-color: #1769e0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px #e4efff; }

components.css: .ds-work-order { list-style: none; background: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #c8d0d6; border-radius: 4px; } .ds-file-header { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 1rem; background: #e9eef1; border-block-end: 1px solid #c8d0d6; } .ds-file-header h3 { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-file-route { display: grid; gap: 0; } .ds-file-route section { padding: 1rem; border-block-end: 1px solid #c8d0d6; } .ds-route-label { margin: 0; color: #52616f; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 750; letter-spacing: 0.055em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-route-value { margin: 0.32rem 0 0; font-weight: 760; } .ds-route-detail { margin: 0.28rem 0 0; color: #52616f; font-size: 0.84rem; } @media (min-width: 46rem) { .ds-file-route { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 0.85fr) minmax(15rem, 1.45fr) minmax(0, 1fr); } .ds-file-route section { border-block-end: 0; border-inline-end: 1px solid #c8d0d6; } .ds-file-route section:last-child { border-inline-end: 0; } }

narrative.overview:
Filetwist reads as a service bench, not an upload card: household media arrives as a work order, gets routed through a visible three-stage path (Original → Profile → Output), and leaves with a stamped, validated result. The instrument header up top always frames what the current work order is and what state it's in, before anything else competes for attention. Panels sit on a deeper "bench" background like tools laid out on a counter, each stamped with a thin accent rule across its top edge, the closest thing this system has to a signature mark.

The palette carries the metaphor: graphite-toned bench surfaces hold pale inspection-sheet panels, blue is reserved for controls and the thing currently happening, amber flags a processing note worth a second look, and green is the seal a file only earns once its output validates. Nothing here is decorative; every color, badge, and stage dot reports a real state from the conversion pipeline. Light and dark are both first-class: the bench darkens to true graphite and panels lighten only relative to it, rather than the whole page inverting to a generic dark theme.
keyCharacteristics: Compact instrument header first; work-order state is visible before scrolling.
A five-stage horizontal path (.job-path) shows literal conversion progress, not a spinner.
Every file becomes a "work order" card with an explicit Original / Profile / Output route.
Color is a state report (blue = active/control, amber = warning, green = validated, red = failed), never mood decoration.
Flat panels lifted by a single soft ambient shadow; buttons press down on click rather than glow.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber (--warn) means "read this before you trust the output"; it never appears on an error. Red (--error) means the operation failed; it never appears on a warning. Green (--ok) is earned only by a passed validation check, a completed stage, or the retention indicator — never a generic "success" toast.

rules.name: The Tabular-Nums Rule
rules.body: Any number that represents a measured fact (byte size, file count, queue depth) uses font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so a work order's figures don't visually jitter as they update over HTMX polling.

rules.name: The Press-Down Rule
rules.body: Every clickable button lifts 1px on hover and drops 1px on :active. A control that doesn't physically respond to a click doesn't belong in this system.

dos: Do treat blue as the only accent for controls, links, and "this is active right now" states (The One Signal Rule).
Do put a 3px accent rule across the top of every instrument panel; it is the system's one recurring signature mark, and it stays static.
Do use monospace tabular-nums for job codes and technical readouts (The Tabular-Nums Rule); use system-font tabular-nums for plain numeric facts like file counts.
Do keep every interactive control at a 44px minimum touch target (--control-size).
Do show conversion progress with the literal 5-stage .job-path tracker rather than an indeterminate spinner whenever a file's route can be described in stages.
donts: Don't use amber (--warn) for a failed operation, or red (--error) for a non-fatal note — the two vocabularies never swap roles.
Don't award a green validation seal for anything short of a passed output check; it is not a generic "done" color.

Don't collapse the three-column Original/Profile/Output route into an unstructured list on desktop; the columns are the story ("bring media in, choose what changes, take the result home") made visible, not a layout convenience.

Don't add a second, heavier elevation style (large drop shadows, glassmorphism, gradients); every surface uses the same flat-with-one-ambient-shadow model (The Press-Down Rule for controls, Panel lift for containers).

Don't open the first viewport with hero imagery, marketing copy, or a generic upload card; the instrument header and current work order state come first, because this is a service bench, not a landing page.
